title: Component Architecture Candidates
purpose: Organize source-influenced reusable presentation relationships that may become typed Kotlin Blueprint contracts after cross-platform pressure, without promoting Android source or Screen Lens projections into portable semantic authority.

sourceSnapshots.role: Canonical VexLife component / experience Blueprint meaning
Android/Kotlin/Compose realization and architectural pressure evidence
Accepted Kotlin semantic/Blueprint authoring, VexWeb relational grammar and deterministic browser artifact generation
Component Library architecture and Screen Lens projection machinery
Materially different desktop music Product with source-owned navigation/selection, stable controls and VexBoard Screen Lens projection

candidates.label: Identity-addressed presentation tree
candidates.question: How can every nested presentation node remain stably addressable across source nesting, runtime realization, tests and Screen Lens without making visual position its identity?
portableRelationships: stable semantic ref survives renderer/framework changes
child identity derives beneath an explicit semantic parent
containment remains inspectable independently of rendered object identity
target source can project the same identity tree back to Screen Lens
obligations: identity must not depend on list index or transient render position
nested custom presentation must not silently lose parent continuity
duplicate identities fail closed
targetPressure: SwiftUI accessibilityIdentifier or equivalent projection hook

sourceEvidence.why: Accepted commonMain Kotlin Blueprint already exposes compiler-visible stable element handles and parent relationships independently of renderer/runtime state.
Nested source topology forms stable element paths and parent relationships.
Custom Compose presentation inherits semantic parent identity and fails closed outside a parent scope.
Platform modifier chains attach already-owned semantic identity without becoming another identity system.
Canonical VexLife components already distinguish stable component/instance/slot identities.
VexStream uses stable region/control refs and parent relationships to project one browser product without a test-only identity registry.
Accepted current Product test proves the authored workspace identity set is unique and verifies exact parentRef relationships without using human labels.
Accepted browser artifact tests preserve source refs as data-vex-ref and source parent/container relationships in the semantic manifest.
Accepted Android tests fail closed on duplicate element identity and recover static parent/Screen ownership independently of runtime view object identity.
Current SwiftUI reference pressure carries the exact source element refs into typed Swift raw identities/accessibility identifiers and the reverse-projection manifest.

candidates.note: Strong first Kotlin Blueprint root law: identity before renderer.

formation.ownerRule: Each Product owns the meaning of its identities; the portable relationship carries stable addressability and source parentage only, never Product state or human-facing words.
portableFields: stableRef: source-owned stable node/element/component identity
sourceParentRef: optional source-owned parent identity
roleOrKind: bounded source-visible structural/presentation role
sourceCoordinate: repository/revision/source path or equivalent provenance coordinate
nonOwnership: target-native accessibility/test mechanism as canonical identity
targetObligations: preserve the stable source identity through generated/native target form
preserve or explicitly map source parentage even when target-native containment differs
fail closed on duplicate source identities
project target identity mapping back through a target manifest or Screen Lens coordinate
acceptanceProofs: same source identities survive at least two materially different target forms
duplicate identity negative case fails deterministically
target projection can reconstruct source ref and parent relationship without parsing human labels
no target-specific object identity is promoted into Product meaning
formation.note: A3 portable identity relationship accepted: VexLife-Prod browser generation preserves source refs and parentage in target artifacts/manifests; SwiftUI reference generation carries the same Product refs into typed Swift identities and reverse-projection metadata; accepted Android BlueprintRegistry tests fail closed on duplicate element identity; accepted Product tests verify current unique refs and exact parent relationships. Portable acceptance covers stable source addressability, source parentage, bounded role/kind and provenance only. DOM attributes, SwiftUI accessibility identifiers and native view-object identity remain target mechanisms under A4.

candidates.label: Semantic control binding
candidates.question: How can a visible control bind to stable action meaning while each platform remains free to choose the appropriate native interaction form?
portableRelationships: control identity is separate from semantic action identity
interaction form may vary without redefining the action
availability/exposure can be projected separately from action meaning
obligations: one stable semantic action/ref is addressable independently of native callback syntax
platform adapter must preserve capability/permission obligations when present
native event wiring cannot become canonical meaning
targetPressure: voice or model-tool expression of the same action
VexStream browser-native source-owned control intent/pathway projection

sourceEvidence.why: Typed intent/action identity is separate from native Compose cells.
VexLife already allows button, native control, menu, vessel, voice and model-tool forms to express stable semantic meaning.
Presentation may change form without becoming semantic truth owner.
VexLife-Prod PR #506 pressure maps current typed Quick Actions relationships to native SwiftUI source while preserving exact source refs and binding meaning in a reverse-projection manifest.
VexStream projects dozens of stable control identities with source-owned intent refs and bounded pathways independently of VexLife/Android widget classes.
Current browser manifestation realizes the typed Quick Actions relationships as native glyph buttons/links and local presentation callbacks while Product/source binding identities remain upstream.
SwiftUI reference test source deliberately supplies an unadmitted Capability binding through the rightful VexWebAuthoring boundary and expects deterministic failure rather than callback invention.

candidates.note: The portable contract should say what action/control relationship exists, not which widget class handles it.

formation.ownerRule: The Product/domain owner defines what an action, capability, local interaction or navigation target means. The portable relationship binds a visible/control identity to that already-owned meaning without owning effects.
portableFields: controlRef: stable source-owned control/element identity
interactionKind: activate/change/resize or another admitted source interaction
bindingKind: source-owned action/capability/local-interaction/navigation relationship
bindingTargetRef: stable source-owned target/action/capability coordinate when one exists
targetObligations: preserve semantic binding independently of native event callback syntax
map every admitted binding kind or return an explicit HELD/PLATFORM_SPECIFIC/UNSUPPORTED disposition
preserve capability/permission boundaries when the Product source owns them
project target event/control realization without making it a second semantic owner
acceptanceProofs: same semantic binding survives materially different interaction forms
target generation rejects or holds unknown binding kinds instead of guessing
target manifestation can be traced back to the exact source control and binding target
effect authority remains outside the presentation mapping
formation.note: A3 portable semantic-control binding accepted: current browser Quick Actions and SwiftUI Menu reference preserve the same source binding meanings across materially different forms; Swift generation carries exact binding targets and keeps host callback/effect execution outside generated presentation; an unadmitted binding kind is rejected rather than guessed; VexStream/Android independently demonstrate stable source-owned control intents/pathways outside these target forms. Acceptance covers controlRef + admitted interactionKind + bindingKind + stable bindingTargetRef only. Effect execution, provider success, native callback identity, words/icons and Apple native proof remain outside A3.

candidates.label: Typed containment and slots
candidates.question: How can source visually communicate what fits inside what while preserving explicit parent/child/slot relationships for target generation and Screen Lens?
portableRelationships: parent owns admitted child/slot topology
source nesting and normalized containment graph agree
layout form and semantic ownership remain distinct
obligations: target adapter preserves child ownership/topology
invalid child placement fails before generation where contract can know it
mustNotOwn: feature state merely because it contains feature presentation

Nested DSL mirrors the intended containment tree and registry can recover parent/children.
Canonical components already expose stable slot relationships independent of rendering technology.
The VexStream Lens recovers source-authored parent/child containment across shell terrain, nested modes and controls in a materially different Product.
Accepted Product test reconstructs exact authored parent relationships for the current nested workspace from compiler-visible Blueprint coordinates.
Android registry tests recover source parentage separately from runtime context and fail closed when a local child/container relationship crosses its admitted Screen ownership.

SwiftUI pressure realizes source collection/trigger/action containment as Menu/label/actions while retaining sourceParentRef and explicit targetRole metadata instead of copying the source tree literally.

candidates.note: This is the composable readability Victor is pointing at: code nesting should carry relationship meaning, not just syntax.

formation.ownerRule: Each Product owns its authored structural/topological relationships. Portable containment preserves source parent/child/slot meaning while allowing target-native manifestation trees to differ when the mapping is explicit.
portableFields: parentRef: stable source container/parent identity
childRefs: admitted direct source child identities
slotRef: optional source-owned semantic slot
placementOrRole: optional source-owned placement/role relationship
nonOwnership: feature/domain state merely because a container presents it
literal target view hierarchy as canonical source topology
targetObligations: preserve direct source parent/child ownership or explicitly record the target realization mapping
preserve source-owned slot identity where present
reject child references outside the admitted source relationship
never infer source ownership solely from the target-native view tree
acceptanceProofs: nested source relationships reconstruct identically from more than one Product
at least one target proves non-literal native containment while preserving source topology
invalid child/parent or slot relationships fail before target acceptance
target Screen Lens/manifest can distinguish source containment from target manifestation containment
formation.note: A3 portable containment accepted: VexLife-Prod and Android compiler-visible trees plus VexStream Lens reconstruct nested source ownership across materially different Products; Android registry source fails closed on cross-container/Screen relationship violations; SwiftUI Quick Actions proves a non-literal native target tree can preserve source parentage through explicit target-role mapping. Acceptance covers source parentRef/direct childRefs/optional slotRef/optional placement-role relationships only. Framework containers, spacing and literal native view hierarchies remain target concerns.

candidates.label: Swappable region
candidates.question: How can one stable region switch among direct child expressions without creating app-navigation depth or duplicating ownership?
portableRelationships: one stable subject/container owns an admitted child-selection relationship
default/initial child identity is explicit
selection owner and current selected child are source-visible
choices bind admitted target child refs to one or more selector refs
choice-set coverage is explicit: EXHAUSTIVE / BOUNDED / UNKNOWN; one Product's direct-child topology must not be used to infer another Product's completeness
a choice may realize additional nested relationships while active
an outer gate may condition the whole local selection without becoming the selected child
selecting a peer child does not automatically create app navigation depth
obligations: selected target must belong to the source-owned admitted choice set
selector identity must remain distinct from selected child identity
multiple selectors for one target must be preserved when source owns them
defaultRef must name an admitted target
EXHAUSTIVE coverage must not omit admitted choices; UNKNOWN coverage must not be promoted to exhaustive
switching does not fabricate screen navigation history
targetPressure: SwiftUI target generation HELD until current Product owns one compiler-visible local selection/default-child relationship
Current VexLife-Prod behavior is split across typed VexWeb structure and browser-local state.view

sourceEvidence.why: Gallery proves peer expressions under one stable region via swapTo rather than screen navigation.
Registry validates direct-child and same-scope SwapTo relationships.

Current typed presentation source establishes one local content container with Conversation/Settings children and a local-interaction switch control, but does not encode the full selected/default-child contract.
Current browser runtime owns the missing local selection facts: default conversation, settings/conversation toggle, mutually exclusive visibility, and no app-navigation depth.

A materially different music Product independently owns one finite local mode set, an explicit default, selected-mode projection and local select(next) without importing Android SwappableContainer source.
VexStream Screen Lens projects the source-owned selection region, its admitted child panels and stable selector controls as one inspectable relationship tree.

candidates.note: Android Gallery and VexStream Discover now independently prove the local-selection law. Current VexLife-Prod has equivalent lived Conversation/Settings behavior but lacks one compiler-visible selected/default-child contract, so SwiftUI generation for that Product remains held rather than inferred from browser state.view.

formation.ownerRule: The Product source owns the local selection meaning/currentness. The reusable relationship carries an admitted child-selection topology and selector mapping without turning local presentation into app navigation or feature-domain state.
portableFields: subjectRef: stable source container/selection subject
defaultRef: explicit admitted initial/default child
choiceCoverage: explicit EXHAUSTIVE / BOUNDED / UNKNOWN coverage of the declared choice set
choices: targetRef plus one-or-more selectorRefs per admitted child

gate: optional outer presence predicate distinct from child selection
realizes: optional source-owned descendant relationships active under a selected child
nonOwnership: outer presence gate as selected-child identity
targetObligations: preserve selector identity separately from selected child identity
preserve multiple selectors for one selected target
preserve explicit choice coverage; UNKNOWN must remain unknown rather than being inferred from child count
never infer default/current selection solely from target runtime visibility strings
keep local selection out of app navigation history unless Product source explicitly says otherwise
acceptanceProofs: Android and VexStream source laws normalize without losing default/current/selector relationships while Android coverage remains UNKNOWN and VexStream preserves EXHAUSTIVE/BOUNDED
current VexLife-Prod forms or binds one compiler-visible default/current local-selection contract before its SwiftUI mapping proceeds
at least one second target maps local selection without creating app navigation depth
many-to-one selector mapping and bounded/non-exhaustive choice sets survive round-trip projection
invalid default/target/selector relationships fail closed
formation.note: A3 formation decision is HELD, not unresolved: Android and VexStream establish the portable Local Selection shape and its coverage/gate/selector pressures, but current VexLife-Prod keeps default/current Conversation-vs-Settings selection split between typed VexWeb structure and browser-local state.view. Accepting or generating SwiftUI from that split would infer canonical meaning from runtime visibility. Victor explicitly deferred production component refactors, so the portable candidate remains held until Product source owns or binds one compiler-visible default/current selection contract. The hold is local to this candidate and does not invalidate the five accepted A3 relationships.

open/close/dismiss remain typed presentation relationships

obligations: target must report how modality was realized
platform-native dismissal maps to modal dismissal rather than fabricating another control activation
mustNotOwn: feature semantic state unless explicitly bound
targetPressure: Current VexLife-Prod ContextInspector: typed Depth.Modal identity + browser-native dialog showModal/close runtime realization
SwiftUI modal generation HELD until opener/dismiss relationship and required-vs-platform-specific modality are compiler-visible

sourceEvidence.why: One semantic/presentation identity is wrapped by distinct Android-native modal realizations.
Gallery carries both modal realization patterns under the same local presentation ownership rules.
Current Product typed presentation source identifies a Context Inspector on the Modal depth plane, but does not bind its open/dismiss controls in the typed relationship source.
Current browser realization chooses native HTML dialog mechanics and wires open/close in runtime JavaScript, exposing a typed-source gap before another target should generate modal behavior.

candidates.note: Current pressure does not yet prove Dialog vs Bottom Sheet is universally portable. The smaller earned need is compiler-visible modal identity + open/dismiss relationship; target-specific modality (.sheet/.alert/.popover/etc.) should remain explicit until Product meaning requires one.

candidates.label: Stable repeated-item collection

targetPressure: VexLife-Prod ConversationTimeline: durable messageRef/eventRef identity + ordinary browser list rebuild
SwiftUI ForEach/List keyed by feature-owned stable item identity
VexLife-Prod #506 exact SwiftUI reference: messageRef -> Identifiable.id / ForEach / View.id
SwiftUI requested-visible / visible-item / scroll-lock relationships remain HELD pending target API proof

sourceEvidence.why: Several materially different Android consumers earned stable repeated-item mechanics independent of feature meaning.
Current Product Blueprint already identifies ConversationTimeline as a collection without making runtime messages static Blueprint elements.
Durable Conversation rows already carry feature-owned stable identity and chronology coordinates independently of visual list position.

Browser realization currently rebuilds ordinary timeline nodes with replaceChildren while separately preserving the mounted live-stream node, exposing real pressure for reusable stable repeated-item mechanics.

VexLife-Prod PR #506 maps the current ConversationTimeline collection + durable messageRef/eventRef/sequence coordinates into SwiftUI stable item identity while explicitly holding unproved viewport mechanics.
Draft PR #261 adds the exact Android insert/remove identity pressure A3 previously held, without changing production component source.

candidates.note: Cross-platform pressure is now real: Android has VexStableLazyColumn; current VexLife-Prod has stable Conversation message identity but ordinary browser renders rebuild the timeline while live streaming requires mounted-node preservation. A portable contract should own stable repeated-item mechanics only, leaving message meaning/order/store with Conversation.

formation.ownerRule: The feature/domain owner supplies item identity, item meaning and ordering. The reusable repeated-item relationship owns only stable presentation identity mechanics and target capability dispositions.

formation.note: A3 Stable Repeated Items accepted from the cross-target intersection: SwiftUI reference runtime proves insert/remove/reorder identity and duplicate-ID failure; exact current VexStream browser identity source proves surviving playlist/trash identity across insert/remove/reorder while preserving caller order and failing blank identity; VexStream Screen Lens projects collection/item identity without list-index reconstruction; optional requested visibility/visible-item/scroll-lock/reuse mechanics remain explicit target dispositions. Android Compose remains a valuable third realization with PR #261 source-formed insert/remove pressure and repository Gradle execution still owed. Acceptance owns collection identity + feature-owned item identity + uniqueness + caller-owned order only; item meaning/store/ordering policy remain with the Product.

candidates.note: Android and VexStream independently establish local navigation as a bounded presentation-location owner beneath one Screen. Android contributes path/depth/back-fallthrough/direction; VexStream contributes open/close plus reconciliation when a durable selected playlist disappears.
